# sudokUI

> sudokUI is a free sudoku app that runs in the browser and teaches you to solve. When you are stuck, a hint names the technique that comes next and, if you ask, walks you through it on your own grid, one step at a time, saying why it works. It works offline once loaded, needs no account and shows no ads. In English, Norwegian and Spanish.

sudokUI is for people who play sudoku and want to get better at it at their own pace: from a beginner meeting their first hidden single to an experienced solver practising X-Wings and chains, or reading up on Exocets. There is no course to follow. You play, look up a technique when you want to, and ask for a hint when you are stuck.

What it does:

- Play sudoku at five difficulty levels, with corner and centre pencil marks, colours, undo, and multi-select on touch screens.
- Hints for 77 solving techniques. A hint names the technique first and shows the step on your own grid only if you ask, and every hint is checked against the puzzle's solution before it is shown.
- Practice for 61 named techniques: pick one and get a puzzle whose next step needs it.
- A solver that names and explains every step of a solution, and a scan that lists every technique that works in the position in front of you.
- A daily puzzle, the same for everyone in the world; after an unassisted solve you can send your time and compare it with everyone else's.
- A difficulty rating for any puzzle, on HoDoKu-compatible scores (with thanks to HoDoKu's author, Bernhard Hobiger).
- Type a puzzle in or scan a photo of one; share puzzles and positions as links or pictures.
- A learning path in the order a solver needs the techniques, showing where you stand from your own games, and a guide to all 80 techniques in plain words.
- It installs from the browser as an app on a phone, a tablet or a computer, and keeps working with no connection.

What it does not do:

- No account, no sign-up, no ads, no paywall, no purchases.
- No leaderboards, followers, feeds or streak rewards.
- No lessons and no course: the guide only suggests what to learn next from your own games; you choose.
- Your games, pencil marks and statistics stay on your device; they leave it only when you share a link or a picture, send a daily time or send a report. The server counts games started and finished, and shares, with no ID and nothing that tells players apart; the privacy page says exactly what is sent.
- It is a web app, not an app-store download.

## Start here

- [Play sudokUI](https://sudokui.app/): the app itself, also in [Norwegian](https://sudokui.app/nb/) and [Spanish](https://sudokui.app/es/)
- [Why sudokUI?](https://sudokui.app/why/): what the app is for and what it promises
- [Privacy](https://sudokui.app/privacy/): exactly what sudokUI sends from your device, and what it never collects

## Learn

- [Sudoku solving techniques](https://sudokui.app/learn/): all 80 techniques explained in plain words, from Naked Single to Exocet, each with its own page
- [How sudoku techniques fit together](https://sudokui.app/learn/intuition/): locked sets, almost locked sets and chains, explained simply
- [Sudoku glossary](https://sudokui.app/learn/glossary/): candidates, strong and weak links, fins, deadly patterns and more
- [How the best sudoku solvers play](https://sudokui.app/how-the-best-solve/): the order champions solve in, and how to train it
- [Sudoku difficulty rating](https://sudokui.app/sudoku-difficulty-rating/): how a puzzle's difficulty is scored, and the five levels
- [Daily sudoku](https://sudokui.app/daily-sudoku/): one puzzle a day, identical for every player
- [Sudoku advent calendar](https://sudokui.app/advent/): a sudoku behind each door in December, from Easy to Extreme, the same for every player
- [Sudoku solver that explains every step](https://sudokui.app/sudoku-solver/): enter any sudoku and see each step named and drawn
